document: GLPG Employee Handbook & HR Self-Service Manual

chunks.sectionTitle: Welcome, Purpose, and Company Snapshot
chunks.text: Welcome to Great Lakes Property Group. This handbook is designed as a practical, question-oriented reference: employees should be able to identify the rule, understand the next step, know who owns the issue, and see the expected response time.

chunks.sectionTitle: Welcome, Purpose, and Company Snapshot
chunks.text: Who this handbook applies to The handbook applies to GLPG W-2 employees unless a section expressly says otherwise. Independent agents, contractors, vendors, and temporary agency workers are governed by their separate written agreements and applicable law; selected safety, information-security, Fair Housing, property-access, and conduct requirements may also apply to them while working with GLPG.

chunks.sectionTitle: Welcome, Purpose, and Company Snapshot
chunks.text: If a signed employment agreement, commission agreement, benefit plan document, or law conflicts with this handbook, the controlling agreement or law governs. Ask People Operations to identify the controlling document.

chunks.sectionTitle: Welcome, Purpose, and Company Snapshot
chunks.sub: What this handbook is—and is not
chunks.text:
• It is the first place to look for routine answers about pay, leave, benefits, conduct, safety, and internal processes.
• It is not an employment contract, guarantee of continued employment, complete legal statement, or substitute for plan documents, transaction procedures, or an individual written agreement.
• It does not limit employees’ rights to discuss wages or working conditions, report concerns to government agencies, participate in protected activity, or make disclosures protected by law.
• Only the Managing Member may approve a company-wide policy exception, and any exception must be written and stored by People Operations.

chunks.sectionTitle: How to Find an Answer and When to Open an HR Ticket
chunks.q: Should I open a ticket for an emergency?
chunks.text: No. For immediate danger, call 911 first. For an urgent building, property, client, or cybersecurity incident, use the emergency contacts in Section 3 and notify your manager as soon as safe. Open a follow-up HR or operations ticket after the immediate risk is controlled.

chunks.sectionTitle: How to Find an Answer and When to Open an HR Ticket
chunks.q: Can I ask a manager instead of HR?
chunks.text: Yes, for routine scheduling, workload, and team questions. Contact People Operations directly for pay, benefits, leave, accommodation, harassment, discrimination, retaliation, privacy, or a concern involving your manager.

chunks.sectionTitle: How to Find an Answer and When to Open an HR Ticket
chunks.q: What if the handbook does not answer my question?
chunks.text: Open an HR ticket and choose “Policy clarification.” People Operations will either answer directly or route the issue to Payroll, Benefits, the Managing Broker, Operations, IT, or leadership.

chunks.sectionTitle: How to Find an Answer and When to Open an HR Ticket
chunks.q: What if the answer I receive conflicts with the handbook?
chunks.text: Ask the responder to identify the controlling policy, plan document, or written exception. Do not rely on an informal verbal assurance for compensation, benefits, or leave approval.

chunks.sectionTitle: Contacts, Service Standards, and Escalation
chunks.text: Use the contact directory below as the single source of truth for this demo. All contacts are fictional.

chunks.sectionTitle: Contacts, Service Standards, and Escalation
chunks.text: These are internal service targets, not guarantees or limits on urgent action. Statutory deadlines and benefit-plan deadlines take priority.

chunks.sectionTitle: Contacts, Service Standards, and Escalation
chunks.text:
• If you do not receive acknowledgment by the target, reply to the ticket once and copy people@glpg-demo.example.
• If there is still no response within one additional business day, contact Jordan Patel at jordan.patel@glpg-demo.example.
• If your concern involves Morgan Ellis or your direct manager, bypass that person and contact Jordan Patel.
• If the issue involves immediate danger, violence, suspected fraud, a data breach, or a live transaction risk, use the urgent phone path rather than waiting for a ticket.

chunks.sectionTitle: Employment Status, Classifications, and Work Locations
chunks.q: Who can change my classification?
chunks.text: People Operations and the Managing Member review classification changes. Managers cannot promise a change in writing or verbally. Classification is based on the actual working relationship and applicable law, not merely the label in a system.

chunks.sectionTitle: Employment Status, Classifications, and Work Locations
chunks.q: Can my work location change?
chunks.text: A manager may propose a schedule or location change. People Operations must approve permanent changes to the assigned work location, remote-work arrangement, or standard weekly schedule and update payroll records where required.

chunks.sectionTitle: Employment Status, Classifications, and Work Locations
chunks.q: What is the workweek?
chunks.text: For timekeeping and overtime administration, the demo workweek is Sunday 12:00 a.m. through Saturday 11:59 p.m. Eastern. The payroll period is biweekly and ends on the Sunday before payday.

chunks.sectionTitle: Equal Opportunity, Respect, and Anti-Harassment
chunks.text: GLPG’s fictional policy prohibits discrimination, harassment, and retaliation. The policy applies to hiring, assignments, pay, training, promotion, discipline, termination, and all work-related settings, including offices, properties, events, travel, calls, texts, and digital channels.

chunks.sectionTitle: Equal Opportunity, Respect, and Anti-Harassment
chunks.text:
• Do not make unwelcome sexual comments, requests, jokes, gestures, or advances; display offensive material; or condition workplace benefits on personal or romantic attention.
• Do not harass or discriminate based on a protected characteristic under applicable law. The demo list includes race, color, religion, national origin, age, disability, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, genetic information, and any other legally protected status.
• Do not retaliate against a person for raising a concern, participating in an investigation, requesting an accommodation, or exercising a legal right.
• Do not assume conduct must be repeated or severe before it can be reported. Report conduct that may violate this policy promptly.

chunks.sectionTitle: Equal Opportunity, Respect, and Anti-Harassment
chunks.q: Can I report anonymously?
chunks.text: The demo company has a confidential reporting web form at https://employee.glpg-demo.example/report. It accepts anonymous submissions. Anonymous reports may limit follow-up questions, so include dates, locations, witnesses, and available records.

chunks.sectionTitle: Equal Opportunity, Respect, and Anti-Harassment
chunks.q: Will HR tell the person I complained about?
chunks.text: HR shares information only with people who need it to assess, investigate, respond, or meet legal obligations. Complete secrecy cannot be promised because a fair process may require disclosure of relevant allegations and evidence.

chunks.sectionTitle: Equal Opportunity, Respect, and Anti-Harassment
chunks.q: What happens after I report?
chunks.text: HR acknowledges the report, assesses immediate safety and interim measures, identifies relevant policies, assigns an impartial reviewer, gathers information, documents findings, decides corrective steps, and checks for retaliation. Not every report requires a formal investigation, but every report receives appropriate triage.

chunks.sectionTitle: Accommodations, Pregnancy-Related Needs, and Religious Practices
chunks.q: How do I request an accommodation?
chunks.text: Email leave@glpg-demo.example or speak privately with Morgan Ellis. You may request an accommodation in plain language; you do not need to use a legal phrase or complete a special form to start the process.

chunks.sectionTitle: Accommodations, Pregnancy-Related Needs, and Religious Practices
chunks.q: What should I include?
chunks.text: Describe the work-related limitation or need, the job task affected, the accommodation you believe may help, and any timing considerations. Do not send detailed medical records to your manager.

chunks.sectionTitle: Accommodations, Pregnancy-Related Needs, and Religious Practices
chunks.q: What happens next?
chunks.text: People Operations will acknowledge within 1 business day, discuss the request with you, identify essential job functions, consider effective options, and communicate a decision or next step. The demo target is to schedule an initial interactive discussion within 3 business days.

chunks.sectionTitle: Accommodations, Pregnancy-Related Needs, and Religious Practices
chunks.q: Can the company ask for documentation?
chunks.text: When permitted by applicable law and reasonably necessary to evaluate the request, HR may ask for limited supporting information. Requests are handled confidentially and separately from ordinary personnel files.

chunks.sectionTitle: Accommodations, Pregnancy-Related Needs, and Religious Practices
chunks.q: What if I need an urgent temporary adjustment?
chunks.text: Tell HR and your manager what is needed immediately. HR will assess an interim measure while the request is reviewed. Do not delay urgent safety or medical care while waiting for approval. No employee will be required to disclose a diagnosis to a coworker or include medical details in a general HR ticket. Applicable law controls all accommodation decisions.

chunks.sectionTitle: Hiring, Background Checks, Onboarding, and Introductory Period
chunks.text:
• All offers must be issued in writing by People Operations or an authorized hiring manager and must identify title, supervisor, location, compensation, classification, anticipated start date, and any contingencies.
• Background checks, reference checks, and any required notices or authorizations must follow applicable law. A conditional offer is not final until stated contingencies are cleared.
• New W-2 employees complete tax forms, work-authorization documentation, direct-deposit instructions, emergency contact information, policy acknowledgments, and required role training.
• New employees receive a laptop or approved device, MFA setup, building access, key-control instructions (if applicable), payroll portal access, and a role-specific onboarding checklist.
• The demo introductory period is 90 calendar days. It is a coaching and onboarding period, not a guarantee of employment for 90 days or a promise that employment will continue afterward.

chunks.sectionTitle: Hiring, Background Checks, Onboarding, and Introductory Period
chunks.q: When will I get system access?
chunks.text: IT targets account setup by 3:00 p.m. on the business day before your start date if People Operations submits a complete request at least 3 business days in advance.

chunks.sectionTitle: Hiring, Background Checks, Onboarding, and Introductory Period
chunks.q: Who do I contact if my first paycheck is wrong?
chunks.text: Email payroll@glpg-demo.example with your pay date, pay period, the amount or hours in question, and a copy of your pay statement. Do not email a full bank-account number.

chunks.sectionTitle: Personnel Files, Privacy, and Employment Verification
chunks.q: Can I see my personnel file?
chunks.text: Submit a written request to people@glpg-demo.example. The demo target is to acknowledge within 2 business days and arrange a supervised review or secure copy within 7 business days, subject to applicable law and permitted redactions.

chunks.sectionTitle: Personnel Files, Privacy, and Employment Verification
chunks.q: Can I update my address or tax withholding?
chunks.text: Update your information in the payroll portal at https://employee.glpg-demo.example/payroll and notify payroll@glpg-demo.example. Submit changes before the payroll cutoff; changes received after cutoff may take effect in the next cycle.

chunks.sectionTitle: Personnel Files, Privacy, and Employment Verification
chunks.q: How do I request employment verification?
chunks.text: Send the recipient’s name, purpose, requested fields, and any signed authorization to people@glpg-demo.example. Standard verification confirms dates of employment and most recent job title. Compensation is released only with written employee authorization or other lawful basis. Access to personnel records is role-based. Medical, accommodation, leave, investigation, payroll, and identity documents are stored separately with restricted access. Employees should not send sensitive personal information through ordinary team chat.

chunks.sectionTitle: Work Schedules, Attendance, Breaks, and Remote Work
chunks.q: Can I work remotely whenever I want?
chunks.text: No. Hybrid or remote work is role-dependent and requires written approval. An approved arrangement is reviewed every 6 months and may be changed with 14 calendar days’ notice where practicable.

chunks.sectionTitle: Work Schedules, Attendance, Breaks, and Remote Work
chunks.q: What if weather closes the office?
chunks.text: The Managing Member or People Operations sends a notice by 6:30 a.m. Eastern through the employee portal and company email. Employees should not travel to a closed office. Remote work may be assigned if the role permits.

chunks.sectionTitle: Work Schedules, Attendance, Breaks, and Remote Work
chunks.q: Can I make up missed hours?
chunks.text: Only with manager approval and in a way that complies with overtime and scheduling rules. Never work off the clock or alter a time record to make a schedule appear compliant.

chunks.sectionTitle: Timekeeping, Overtime, and Payroll
chunks.text:
• Nonexempt employees record start time, stop time, and meal periods each workday in the payroll portal.
• Enter time by 10:00 a.m. Monday following the end of each pay period. Managers approve by 3:00 p.m. Monday.
• Never work before clocking in, after clocking out, during an unpaid meal period, or from home without recording the time.
• Report a missed punch or incorrect entry to your manager and payroll@glpg-demo.example before Monday noon after the pay period ends.
• All overtime must be approved in advance by the manager. All hours actually worked must still be recorded and will be paid in accordance with applicable law even if not preapproved.

chunks.sectionTitle: Timekeeping, Overtime, and Payroll
chunks.q: What if payday falls on a bank holiday?
chunks.text: The demo payroll is deposited on the preceding business day. Payroll will publish any exception at least 5 business days in advance.

chunks.sectionTitle: Timekeeping, Overtime, and Payroll
chunks.q: My deposit is missing. What should I do?
chunks.text: Check the pay statement and bank account details first. If the deposit is not visible by 12:00 p.m. Eastern on payday, contact Dana Brooks at (734) 555-0143 or payroll@glpg-demo.example.

chunks.sectionTitle: Timekeeping, Overtime, and Payroll
chunks.q: Can my manager ask me not to report overtime?
chunks.text: No. Employees must accurately report all hours worked. Report any instruction to work off the clock to People Operations immediately.

chunks.sectionTitle: Timekeeping, Overtime, and Payroll
chunks.q: How are deductions handled?
chunks.text: Required taxes and legally required deductions are withheld. Voluntary deductions require the applicable authorization. Questions about a deduction should include the pay date, deduction label, and amount.

chunks.sectionTitle: Compensation, Bonuses, Commissions, and Referrals
chunks.text: W-2 employee compensation Base pay is stated in the employee’s offer letter. Changes require written approval from the Managing Member and People Operations. Bonus plans, if any, are governed by their written plan terms, including eligibility, measurement period, approval, payment timing, and treatment at separation.

chunks.sectionTitle: Compensation, Bonuses, Commissions, and Referrals
chunks.text: Independent agent commissions The following is a fictional example only and does not replace an agent’s signed independent contractor or commission agreement.

chunks.sectionTitle: Compensation, Bonuses, Commissions, and Referrals
chunks.q: When will my commission be paid?
chunks.text: The target is 5 business days after all four conditions are met: closing has occurred, brokerage funds have cleared, the transaction file is complete, and the Managing Broker has approved it. If any condition is missing, the payment clock has not started.

chunks.sectionTitle: Compensation, Bonuses, Commissions, and Referrals
chunks.q: Who explains a commission deduction?
chunks.text: Contact commissions@glpg-demo.example and identify the property address or internal transaction ID, closing date, gross commission, and the line item you are questioning.

chunks.sectionTitle: Compensation, Bonuses, Commissions, and Referrals
chunks.q: Can I rely on the 70/30 split if my agreement says something else?
chunks.text: No. Your signed written agreement controls. The 70/30 figure is a default demonstration example only.

chunks.sectionTitle: Expense Reimbursement, Travel, and Company Cards
chunks.q: How do I submit an expense?
chunks.text: Use the Expenses tile in the employee portal, select the business purpose and cost center, enter date and amount, attach receipts, and submit to your manager. Payroll/Finance targets reimbursement in the next regular pay cycle after approval.

chunks.sectionTitle: Expense Reimbursement, Travel, and Company Cards
chunks.q: I lost a receipt. Can I still claim the expense?
chunks.text: Submit a missing-receipt declaration with the vendor, date, amount, business purpose, and reason the receipt is unavailable. Reimbursement is not guaranteed and may require Managing Member approval.

chunks.sectionTitle: Expense Reimbursement, Travel, and Company Cards
chunks.q: Can I use my own car to visit a property?
chunks.text: Only if your manager approves business use and you maintain a valid license, required insurance, and a safe vehicle. Record business miles separately from commuting.

chunks.sectionTitle: Paid Time Off and Vacation
chunks.text:
• Submit the request in the employee portal at least 7 calendar days before a 1–2 day absence and at least 21 calendar days before an absence of 3 or more consecutive workdays.
• Your manager responds within 3 business days. If there is no response, the request is not approved; follow up before making nonrefundable plans.
• Requests are reviewed based on staffing, coverage, business needs, fairness, and prior approved absences. The company will not discriminate or retaliate in scheduling decisions.
• Before taking leave, document urgent work, handoffs, client deadlines, property access coverage, and a contact for time-sensitive matters.

chunks.sectionTitle: Paid Time Off and Vacation
chunks.q: What is the PTO balance cap?
chunks.text: The maximum carry balance is 160 hours. Accrual pauses when the balance reaches 160 hours and resumes after the balance falls below the cap.

chunks.sectionTitle: Paid Time Off and Vacation
chunks.q: Does unused PTO pay out when I leave?
chunks.text: For this demo, accrued unused PTO is paid at separation where required by applicable law or a written agreement; otherwise the demo default is no payout. Because this area is highly location-specific, a real employer must have counsel review the rule before use.

chunks.sectionTitle: Paid Time Off and Vacation
chunks.q: Can I use PTO in hourly increments?
chunks.text: Yes. The minimum request increment is 1 hour, except where a more protective law or approved accommodation requires a different increment.

chunks.sectionTitle: Paid Time Off and Vacation
chunks.q: Can a manager cancel approved PTO?
chunks.text: Only for an unusual, documented business emergency. The manager must consult People Operations, explain the reason, and work with the employee on replacement dates or other available options.

chunks.sectionTitle: Holidays, Sick Time, and Unexpected Absences
chunks.text: If a fixed-date holiday falls on Saturday, the preceding Friday is observed. If it falls on Sunday, the following Monday is observed. The annual holiday calendar is published by December 1 of the prior year. The next year’s exact dates are listed in Appendix B.

chunks.sectionTitle: Holidays, Sick Time, and Unexpected Absences
chunks.q: I am scheduled to work on a holiday. What happens?
chunks.text: Your manager must notify you at least 14 calendar days in advance where practicable. The demo policy provides an alternative paid day off within 30 calendar days or holiday premium pay of 1.5 times the employee’s regular rate for hours worked, whichever the written role schedule specifies. Applicable law and written plan terms control.

chunks.sectionTitle: Holidays, Sick Time, and Unexpected Absences
chunks.q: What if I wake up sick?
chunks.text: Notify your manager at least 30 minutes before your shift when practicable, then record the absence in the employee portal by the end of the day. If you cannot access the portal, email leave@glpg-demo.example.

chunks.sectionTitle: Holidays, Sick Time, and Unexpected Absences
chunks.q: Do I need to share my diagnosis?
chunks.text: No. Do not send a diagnosis to your manager. HR may request limited documentation only when permitted and reasonably necessary.

chunks.sectionTitle: Holidays, Sick Time, and Unexpected Absences
chunks.q: Can I use sick time for a family member?
chunks.text: The demo sick-time bank may be used for the employee’s illness, preventive care, medical appointments, or care for an eligible family member, subject to applicable law and available balance. Demo sick-time bank Full-time employees receive 40 hours of sick time each January 1. Part-time employees scheduled for 20–29 hours receive a pro rata amount. Up to 40 unused hours carry over, but the annual use cap is 40 hours under this demo setting. This is a simulated rule only; actual state and local paid-sick-leave requirements may be more generous.

chunks.sectionTitle: Family, Medical, Bereavement, Civic, and Other Leave
chunks.text: This table is a demonstration configuration, not a statement of legal entitlement. Leave eligibility, duration, pay, documentation, reinstatement, benefit continuation, notice, and concurrency must be reviewed under the laws applicable to the employee and company.

chunks.sectionTitle: Family, Medical, Bereavement, Civic, and Other Leave
chunks.q: How do I request family or medical leave?
chunks.text: Email leave@glpg-demo.example with the anticipated start date, expected duration if known, and best way to reach you. Do not send detailed medical records in the first email.

chunks.sectionTitle: Family, Medical, Bereavement, Civic, and Other Leave
chunks.q: When should I notify HR?
chunks.text: For foreseeable leave, the demo target is 30 calendar days’ notice. For an unexpected event, notify HR as soon as practicable. If there is an emergency, notice may be given by a family member or representative.

chunks.sectionTitle: Family, Medical, Bereavement, Civic, and Other Leave
chunks.q: Can I be required to use PTO during unpaid leave?
chunks.text: The demo default is that available PTO may run concurrently with unpaid leave where permitted by law and plan terms. HR will confirm the sequence in writing before leave begins.

chunks.sectionTitle: Family, Medical, Bereavement, Civic, and Other Leave
chunks.q: What happens to benefits while I am on leave?
chunks.text: HR will provide a written benefits continuation notice, payment amount, due dates, and consequences of missed payments before leave begins or as soon as practicable.

chunks.sectionTitle: Benefits, Enrollment, Dependents, and Retirement
chunks.q: Where do I enroll?
chunks.text: Use Benefits in the employee portal at https://employee.glpg-demo.example/benefits. If the tile is unavailable, email benefits@glpg-demo.example.

chunks.sectionTitle: Benefits, Enrollment, Dependents, and Retirement
chunks.q: I got married / had a child / lost other coverage. What do I do?
chunks.text: Notify benefits@glpg-demo.example within 30 calendar days and upload the event documentation requested by the plan administrator. Do not assume the change is complete until you receive written confirmation.

chunks.sectionTitle: Benefits, Enrollment, Dependents, and Retirement
chunks.q: Where can I find the real plan rules?
chunks.text: The official summary plan descriptions, insurance certificates, and carrier documents control. This manual is only a high-level fictional summary.

chunks.sectionTitle: Benefits, Enrollment, Dependents, and Retirement
chunks.q: When is the 401(k) match paid?
chunks.text: The demo match is calculated each payroll and deposited after payroll close, subject to plan terms, eligibility, vesting, and correction procedures. Questions go to benefits@glpg-demo.example.

chunks.sectionTitle: Benefits, Enrollment, Dependents, and Retirement
chunks.q: Who can see my beneficiary information?
chunks.text: Only authorized benefits personnel and plan administrators with a business need. Keep beneficiary designations current in the plan portal.

chunks.sectionTitle: Workers’ Compensation and Return to Work
chunks.q: What if I am injured at work or while visiting a property?
chunks.text: For emergency care, call 911. As soon as safe, notify your manager and People Operations at people@glpg-demo.example. Submit an incident report within 24 hours, even if the injury seems minor.

chunks.sectionTitle: Workers’ Compensation and Return to Work
chunks.q: What information goes in the incident report?
chunks.text: Date, time, location, task being performed, what happened, witnesses, immediate response, photos if appropriate, and whether medical attention was sought. Do not speculate about fault.

chunks.sectionTitle: Workers’ Compensation and Return to Work
chunks.q: Can I return with restrictions?
chunks.text: Provide work restrictions to People Operations, not the team chat. HR and your manager will review safe temporary duties and any accommodation needs before you resume affected tasks.

chunks.sectionTitle: Workers’ Compensation and Return to Work
chunks.q: Can I use my own health insurance?
chunks.text: Workers’ compensation reporting and claim routing must follow the designated carrier process. HR will provide the fictional carrier contact and claim number after the report is received.

chunks.sectionTitle: Standards of Conduct and Professionalism
chunks.q: What is the dress standard?
chunks.text: Business casual is the default for office work. For client meetings, showings, inspections, and public events, wear clean, professional clothing appropriate to the activity and safe footwear. Managers may set role-specific standards, subject to accommodation and anti-discrimination requirements.

chunks.sectionTitle: Standards of Conduct and Professionalism
chunks.q: Can I accept a gift from a client or vendor?
chunks.text: You may accept a modest promotional item valued at $50 or less if it creates no expectation of preferential treatment. Cash, gift cards over $25, travel, entertainment over $100, or anything tied to a referral, contract award, or transaction requires written Managing Broker approval before acceptance.

chunks.sectionTitle: Standards of Conduct and Professionalism
chunks.q: Can I use company property for personal reasons?
chunks.text: Incidental use of office supplies or internet is permitted if lawful, infrequent, low-cost, does not interfere with work, and creates no security or reputational risk. Company devices and accounts remain subject to monitoring consistent with applicable law and disclosed notices.

chunks.sectionTitle: Conflicts of Interest, Gifts, Outside Work, and Nepotism
chunks.text:
• Disclose any personal, financial, family, or outside business interest that could influence a company decision or transaction.
• Do not steer a client, tenant, vendor, or applicant to a business in which you or a family member has an undisclosed financial interest.
• Do not use confidential company information, work time, company equipment, or client relationships to compete with GLPG.
• Outside employment is permitted if it does not impair performance, create a conflict, misuse company information, or violate a written agreement. Disclose potential conflicts to People Operations.
• Relatives may work at GLPG, but may not directly supervise, evaluate, set compensation for, or approve expenses of one another without a documented alternative reporting arrangement.

chunks.sectionTitle: Conflicts of Interest, Gifts, Outside Work, and Nepotism
chunks.q: I have a side real-estate business. Do I need approval?
chunks.text: Yes. Before accepting outside brokerage, property-management, consulting, or referral work, submit a written disclosure to Avery Chen and People Operations. The Managing Broker will review licensing, client conflicts, brokerage obligations, and use of company resources.

chunks.sectionTitle: Conflicts of Interest, Gifts, Outside Work, and Nepotism
chunks.q: What if I discover a conflict after a transaction starts?
chunks.text: Pause the affected decision where safe, disclose the facts promptly to compliance@glpg-demo.example, and do not conceal or self-approve the conflict.

chunks.sectionTitle: Confidentiality, Records, and Client Information
chunks.text:
• Access client, tenant, applicant, employee, financial, and transaction information only for a legitimate assigned business purpose.
• Use approved systems to store documents. Do not store sensitive records in personal email, personal cloud drives, unapproved messaging apps, or removable media.
• Verify recipient identity and email addresses before sending financial, identity, lease, or transaction documents.
• Do not discuss a client’s financial, family, disability, immigration, or housing circumstances in public spaces or with unauthorized colleagues.
• Report misdirected email, lost devices, exposed documents, or suspected unauthorized access to security@glpg-demo.example immediately.

chunks.sectionTitle: Confidentiality, Records, and Client Information
chunks.q: Can I share a listing or tenant story on social media?
chunks.text: Only if the content is approved for public release, does not identify a client or resident without documented permission, does not reveal access/security details, and complies with Fair Housing, advertising, privacy, and brokerage rules.

chunks.sectionTitle: Confidentiality, Records, and Client Information
chunks.q: How do I correct a record?
chunks.text: Do not overwrite or delete an official record to hide an error. Use the approved correction or amendment function, retain the audit trail, and notify your manager or compliance contact.

chunks.sectionTitle: Technology, AI Tools, Cybersecurity, and Social Media
chunks.text:
• Use unique passwords and multi-factor authentication (MFA) on all company accounts. Never share passwords or approve an MFA prompt you did not initiate.
• Lock your screen whenever you step away. Report lost devices immediately.
• Do not install unapproved software, browser extensions, remote-access tools, or AI plug-ins on company devices.
• Company systems may be monitored for security, operations, and compliance consistent with applicable law and notices.
• Personal use must be limited, lawful, and must not interfere with work or compromise security.

chunks.sectionTitle: Technology, AI Tools, Cybersecurity, and Social Media
chunks.text:
• Use only company-approved AI tools for business tasks.
• Never enter nonpublic client data, tenant records, employee information, financial account details, access codes, credentials, or confidential transaction documents into a public AI tool.
• AI-generated content must be checked by a qualified employee before it is sent, published, used for a housing decision, or added to an official record.
• Do not use AI to make or recommend tenant-screening, hiring, lending, pricing, or other consequential decisions without documented company approval and legal/compliance review.
• Disclose AI assistance when required by company procedure, client agreement, law, or platform terms.

chunks.sectionTitle: Technology, AI Tools, Cybersecurity, and Social Media
chunks.q: I clicked a suspicious link. What now?
chunks.text: Do not enter credentials or continue interacting. Disconnect from the network if IT directs you, call IT at (734) 555-0145, and email security@glpg-demo.example from a safe device. Include the time, device, sender, and what you clicked. Do not delete the message.

chunks.sectionTitle: Technology, AI Tools, Cybersecurity, and Social Media
chunks.q: I received new wire instructions. Can I follow them?
chunks.text: No. Treat any changed wiring instructions as high risk. Verify by calling a previously known, independently sourced phone number—not a number in the email. Require two-person verification by the transaction lead and Managing Broker before any change is acted upon.

chunks.sectionTitle: Technology, AI Tools, Cybersecurity, and Social Media
chunks.q: Can I post personal opinions online?
chunks.text: Employees may engage in lawful personal expression and protected activity. Do not imply you speak for GLPG unless authorized, disclose confidential information, threaten or harass others, or publish nonpublic client/property information.

chunks.sectionTitle: Fair Housing, Accessibility, and Ethical Real Estate Practice
chunks.text: Fair Housing obligations are central to the fictional business. Employees and agents must not discriminate in advertising, showing access, tenant screening, leasing, sales, property management, service requests, or any housing-related decision.

chunks.sectionTitle: Fair Housing, Accessibility, and Ethical Real Estate Practice
chunks.text:
• Use consistent, objective, documented criteria for inquiries, applications, screening, showing access, and service requests.
• Do not make assumptions about a person’s ability, family, language, source of income, or preferences based on a protected characteristic.
• Do not use coded language, steering, selective information, selective follow-up, or different standards for similarly situated people.
• Make reasonable accommodation and modification requests available to the designated property-management contact; do not reject or negotiate such requests independently.
• Use approved listing descriptions and advertising templates. Review photos, captions, audience targeting, and distribution channels for discriminatory language or effect.
• Escalate suspected discrimination, accessibility concerns, or inconsistent treatment to compliance@glpg-demo.example immediately.

chunks.sectionTitle: Fair Housing, Accessibility, and Ethical Real Estate Practice
chunks.q: A tenant asks for an accommodation. What should I do?
chunks.text: Acknowledge the request respectfully, do not ask intrusive questions, do not promise or deny the request, and forward it to operations@glpg-demo.example and compliance@glpg-demo.example the same business day.

chunks.sectionTitle: Fair Housing, Accessibility, and Ethical Real Estate Practice
chunks.q: Can I tell a prospective tenant that a neighborhood is “good for families”?
chunks.text: Do not characterize neighborhoods or properties using protected-class or family-status language. Provide neutral, objective property facts and direct the person to independent public sources for neighborhood information.

chunks.sectionTitle: Fair Housing, Accessibility, and Ethical Real Estate Practice
chunks.q: What if a client requests a discriminatory preference?
chunks.text: Do not follow the instruction. Explain that GLPG uses lawful, consistent criteria and immediately consult the Managing Broker.

chunks.sectionTitle: Licensing, Training, and Continuing Education
chunks.text:
• Employees and agents must maintain any license, registration, certification, or permit required for their assigned duties.
• Provide renewal evidence to compliance@glpg-demo.example at least 30 calendar days before expiration.
• Do not perform a regulated activity while a required credential is expired, suspended, restricted, or otherwise invalid.
• Complete assigned annual training by December 15. The demo annual minimum is 4 hours of compliance training, 2 hours of cybersecurity training, and role-specific safety training.
• Training completion is recorded in the employee portal. If a course is inaccessible or unavailable, open an HR/IT ticket within 2 business days.

chunks.sectionTitle: Licensing, Training, and Continuing Education
chunks.q: Who pays for required licensing?
chunks.text: The demo company reimburses preapproved role-required licensing and renewal costs up to $500 per calendar year for employees. Agents follow their written affiliation agreement. Submit proof of payment and approval within 30 days.

chunks.sectionTitle: Licensing, Training, and Continuing Education
chunks.q: What if my license is about to expire?
chunks.text: Notify the Managing Broker immediately, stop any activity requiring an active license if it expires, and provide the renewal confirmation before resuming the regulated activity.

chunks.sectionTitle: Property Access, Keys, Showings, Vendors, and Resident Interactions
chunks.q: Can I enter a unit if I have a master key?
chunks.text: Only with lawful authorization and a documented business purpose. A master key is not blanket permission. Follow the lease, notice rules, emergency exception requirements, and company entry log.

chunks.sectionTitle: Property Access, Keys, Showings, Vendors, and Resident Interactions
chunks.q: What if a resident refuses entry?
chunks.text: Do not argue or force entry. Leave unless an emergency exception clearly applies, document the interaction, and contact Property Operations for next steps.

chunks.sectionTitle: Property Access, Keys, Showings, Vendors, and Resident Interactions
chunks.q: Can I send an access code by text?
chunks.text: Only through the approved secure system and only to an authorized recipient. Never send codes to an unverified number or in a public group chat.

chunks.sectionTitle: Field Safety, Driving, Lone Work, and Emergencies
chunks.text:
• Check the property address, appointment details, known hazards, access instructions, and emergency contact.
• Tell a colleague or manager where you are going and your expected check-in time for vacant, remote, or higher-risk properties.
• Carry a charged phone, keep keys secure, and park in a well-lit location where possible.
• Do not enter if you observe signs of forced entry, weapons, aggressive animals, hazardous materials, structural instability, or threatening behavior.

chunks.sectionTitle: Field Safety, Driving, Lone Work, and Emergencies
chunks.q: What if I feel unsafe during a showing?
chunks.text: Leave immediately if possible. Do not confront the person. Move to a safe public location and call 911 if threatened or in danger. Notify your manager and Operations as soon as safe.

chunks.sectionTitle: Field Safety, Driving, Lone Work, and Emergencies
chunks.q: What if there is a fire, gas smell, or carbon monoxide alarm?
chunks.text: Evacuate; do not investigate or re-enter. Call 911 or the utility emergency number from a safe location. Notify Operations after emergency services are contacted.

chunks.sectionTitle: Field Safety, Driving, Lone Work, and Emergencies
chunks.q: What if I am in a car accident on company business?
chunks.text: Check for injuries and call 911 if needed. Exchange required information, do not admit fault, photograph the scene if safe, notify your manager, and submit an incident report within 24 hours.

chunks.sectionTitle: Field Safety, Driving, Lone Work, and Emergencies
chunks.q: Can I drive while using my phone hands-free?
chunks.text: Do not handle a phone while driving. Pull over safely before calling, texting, entering directions, or responding to messages.

chunks.sectionTitle: Performance Reviews, Coaching, and Development
chunks.q: What is evaluated?
chunks.text: Role-specific outcomes, quality, reliability, collaboration, client service, compliance, safety, and progress against agreed goals. Evaluation should rely on job-related examples and documented expectations.

chunks.sectionTitle: Performance Reviews, Coaching, and Development
chunks.q: Can I disagree with my review?
chunks.text: Yes. Add written comments in the review system within 5 business days or send them to people@glpg-demo.example. The comments are attached to the review record.

chunks.sectionTitle: Performance Reviews, Coaching, and Development
chunks.q: Is a review a promise of a raise or promotion?
chunks.text: No. Compensation and promotion decisions require separate approval and written communication.

chunks.sectionTitle: Corrective Action and Performance Improvement Plans
chunks.text: The demo company generally uses progressive corrective action to clarify expectations, support improvement, and address repeated or serious issues. The steps are a guide, not a guarantee that every case will follow every step.

chunks.sectionTitle: Corrective Action and Performance Improvement Plans
chunks.text: Serious misconduct—such as violence, theft, harassment, deliberate falsification, major safety violations, or serious confidentiality breaches—may result in immediate action, including termination, without earlier steps. Employment remains at will to the extent permitted by law.

chunks.sectionTitle: Corrective Action and Performance Improvement Plans
chunks.q: What should a fair PIP include?
chunks.text: The issue described with specific examples; measurable expectations; resources and training; owner for support; start and end dates; weekly check-in schedule; how progress is measured; and potential next steps if expectations are not met.

chunks.sectionTitle: Corrective Action and Performance Improvement Plans
chunks.q: How long is a PIP?
chunks.text: The demo default is 60 calendar days, with weekly check-ins. HR may approve a 30-day or 90-day plan based on the role and issue. Any extension must be written.

chunks.sectionTitle: Corrective Action and Performance Improvement Plans
chunks.q: Can I respond to a warning?
chunks.text: Yes. You may submit a written response within 5 business days. People Operations attaches it to the corrective-action record.

chunks.sectionTitle: Complaints, Investigations, and Non-Retaliation
chunks.sub: Employee rights and responsibilities during a review
chunks.text:
• Provide truthful information and preserve relevant records. Do not delete messages, alter files, or coordinate stories.
• Do not retaliate, threaten, pressure, or interfere with a reporter, witness, or investigator.
• Maintain reasonable confidentiality. Do not discuss details with coworkers who have no need to know; this does not restrict legally protected discussions or reporting.
• Tell HR if you believe the assigned investigator has a conflict or if you experience retaliation.
• Ask for clarification if you do not understand a question or need an accommodation to participate.

chunks.sectionTitle: Complaints, Investigations, and Non-Retaliation
chunks.q: Will I be told the outcome?
chunks.sub: Employee rights and responsibilities during a review
chunks.text: The reporter and subject will generally receive confirmation that the review is complete and that appropriate action has been taken, to the extent permitted. Private personnel details and discipline imposed on another employee are not normally shared.

chunks.sectionTitle: Complaints, Investigations, and Non-Retaliation
chunks.q: Can I bring someone to an interview?
chunks.sub: Employee rights and responsibilities during a review
chunks.text: For a routine fact-finding meeting, the demo default is an individual interview. If you believe you have a legal or contractual right to representation, or need an accommodation, tell HR before the meeting. Applicable law and agreements control.

chunks.sectionTitle: Complaints, Investigations, and Non-Retaliation
chunks.q: How long will an investigation take?
chunks.sub: Employee rights and responsibilities during a review
chunks.text: The demo target is to complete routine matters within 20 business days after intake. Complex matters, unavailable witnesses, external proceedings, or safety issues may take longer. HR provides an update at least every 10 business days while the matter remains open.

chunks.sectionTitle: Complaints, Investigations, and Non-Retaliation
chunks.q: What if I disagree with the outcome?
chunks.sub: Employee rights and responsibilities during a review
chunks.text: Send a written request for reconsideration to Jordan Patel within 5 business days of the closure notice, identifying a material factual error, new evidence, or process concern. Reconsideration is not a re-investigation by default.

chunks.sectionTitle: Workplace Violence, Substance Use, and Threat Response
chunks.text:
• Threats, intimidation, stalking, physical violence, possession or use of prohibited weapons at work, and deliberate property damage are prohibited, subject to applicable law.
• Do not report to work impaired by alcohol, illegal drugs, or misuse of medication in a way that creates a safety risk. Employees using prescribed medication may request a confidential accommodation without disclosing details to coworkers.
• Smoking and vaping are prohibited inside company offices, vehicles, and properties where prohibited by law or lease. Follow posted property rules.
• Report threats, suspicious conduct, or safety concerns to a manager and People Operations. Call 911 for immediate danger.
• Do not attempt to physically intervene in a violent incident unless necessary to protect yourself from imminent harm.

chunks.sectionTitle: Workplace Violence, Substance Use, and Threat Response
chunks.q: What if I see a weapon or receive a threat?
chunks.text: Move to safety, call 911 if there is an immediate threat, notify the manager and People Operations, and provide the exact words/actions, time, location, and any witnesses when safe.

chunks.sectionTitle: Workplace Violence, Substance Use, and Threat Response
chunks.q: Can the company conduct a drug test?
chunks.text: Only under a written testing protocol and when permitted by applicable law. People Operations will provide the reason, process, privacy protections, and any review rights.

chunks.sectionTitle: Separation, Final Pay, and Offboarding
chunks.q: Do I have to give two weeks’ notice?
chunks.text: Two weeks is requested to support transition planning. It is not a condition of receiving earned wages or other rights under applicable law.

chunks.sectionTitle: Separation, Final Pay, and Offboarding
chunks.q: When will I receive my final pay?
chunks.text: The demo target is the next regular payday. If your work location’s law requires a different deadline, that legal deadline controls. Contact payroll@glpg-demo.example for a written final-pay calculation.

chunks.sectionTitle: Separation, Final Pay, and Offboarding
chunks.q: What happens to my benefits?
chunks.text: Benefits will end or continue according to plan terms and applicable law. HR provides a written notice with coverage end date, continuation options, election deadlines, and contact information.

chunks.sectionTitle: Separation, Final Pay, and Offboarding
chunks.q: Can I keep client files or transaction documents?
chunks.text: No. Company and client records remain with GLPG unless a written agreement or law provides otherwise. Do not forward records to personal email or retain copies without authorization.

chunks.sectionTitle: Records Retention, Policy Changes, and Questions
chunks.text:
• Employees must preserve business records in approved systems and follow legal holds, audit instructions, and retention schedules.
• Do not delete or alter records subject to an investigation, dispute, claim, audit, or legal hold.
• People Operations reviews the handbook at least annually each October and whenever a material policy, law, benefit plan, or operational process changes.
• Revisions are published in the employee portal with a version number, effective date, and summary of material changes.
• Employees receive notice of material changes and may be asked to acknowledge receipt again.

chunks.sectionTitle: Records Retention, Policy Changes, and Questions
chunks.q: Which version applies?
chunks.text: The current version in the employee portal controls for demo purposes. Downloaded or printed copies may be outdated.

chunks.sectionTitle: Records Retention, Policy Changes, and Questions
chunks.q: Can a manager change a policy?
chunks.text: No. Managers may propose changes but cannot amend company-wide policy. Only the Managing Member approves policy changes, with People Operations maintaining the controlled version.

chunks.sectionTitle: Records Retention, Policy Changes, and Questions
chunks.q: Does this handbook create a contract?
chunks.text: No. It is a policy guide and not an employment contract or guarantee of employment. At-will status applies to the extent permitted by law and may be changed only by a written agreement signed by the Managing Member.

chunks.sectionTitle: HR Ticket Submission Guide and Required Details
chunks.text:
• The relevant date(s), location, pay period, transaction ID, or property identifier.
• What happened, what you expected, and what you have already tried.
• The specific decision or answer you need.
• Relevant documents attached through the approved secure portal—not sensitive credentials or full bank-account numbers.

chunks.sectionTitle: HR Ticket Submission Guide and Required Details
chunks.sub: Do not use an ordinary HR ticket for
chunks.text:
• An immediate emergency or threat: call 911 first.
• A live wire-fraud attempt or active data breach: call IT Security and the Managing Broker immediately.
• An urgent property-access or safety issue: call Property Operations.
• A request to conceal, delete, or alter records: preserve the records and contact People Operations.

chunks.sectionTitle: Forms, Checklists, and Acknowledgment
chunks.text:
• Offer letter and classification confirmed; start date and manager identified.
• Work authorization, tax, direct deposit, emergency contact, and required forms completed.
• Handbook and anti-harassment policy received; acknowledgment submitted.
• Payroll, benefits, IT, MFA, and employee portal access verified.
• Role-specific training completed: privacy, cybersecurity, Fair Housing (where relevant), property access, safety, and records handling.
• Equipment, keys, access credentials, and asset log completed.

chunks.sectionTitle: Forms, Checklists, and Acknowledgment
chunks.text:
• Date/time/location; people involved; task being performed.
• Factual description in chronological order; exact words if relevant.
• Witnesses and available photos, messages, documents, or video.
• Immediate action taken; emergency services or medical care contacted.
• Manager/HR/Operations notified and time of notification.
• Do not speculate, assign blame, or alter original evidence.

chunks.text: The dates above are a fictional calendar example. The annual calendar is published by December 1 of the prior year. Any change is announced through the employee portal and company email.
